item.title: Naoshima Art Island: A Day Trip from Okayama — Guide
item.description: Naoshima is a small island in the Seto Inland Sea that has become one of the most celebrated contemporary art destinations on earth. From the 1990s, the Benesse corporation and architect Tadao Ando remade it: concrete museums are sunk into the hillsides so as not to intrude on the landscape, works by Monet, Turrell and De Maria sit in purpose-built chambers, Yayoi Kusama’s spotted pumpkins stand on the piers, and in the village of Honmura old wooden houses have been converted into individual artworks.

item.title: Hyogo Prefectural Museum of Art: Tadao Ando on the Waterfront — Guide
item.description: The Hyogo Prefectural Museum of Art is the largest art museum in western Japan and as much an architectural destination as an art one: its building, completed in 2002 by Tadao Ando, is a monumental composition of raw concrete, glass volumes and open external stairways stepping down to the Kobe waterfront, built as part of the city’s cultural recovery after the 1995 Great Hanshin earthquake. The collection spans modern Japanese and Western sculpture, prints and painting, and even without a ticket the terraces, stairways and sea-facing spaces are free to explore.

item.title: Akita Museum of Art: Foujita's Mural & Tadao Ando — Guide
item.description: The Akita Museum of Art, designed by Tadao Ando, is home to Tsuguharu Foujita’s monumental mural ‘Events in Akita’ — one of the largest canvases in Japan, depicting the prefecture’s festivals and daily life. Ando’s spiral staircase and a rooftop triangular water pool that frames Senshu Park make the building itself a work of art. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Akita City, Akita Hours ~10:00–18:00 (closed irregular) Admission Around ¥310 (collection) Time needed About 1 hour Best time Year-round What to See Foujita’s vast mural ‘Events in Akita’.

item.title: Naoshima Art Island, Kagawa: The Complete Visitor's Guide
item.description: Naoshima is a small island of roughly 8 square kilometres in the Seto Inland Sea, about 50 minutes by ferry from Takamatsu. In the early 1990s, it was a quiet island with an ageing fishing population, a modest industrial presence, and no particular reason to appear on any travel itinerary. Over the following three decades, the Fukutake Foundation — the philanthropic arm of Benesse Holdings, based in Okayama — transformed it into one of the world’s most celebrated destinations for contemporary art and architecture.
